keyEvents.event: Revolution brings Fidel Castro to power
keyEvents.impact: Founded a one-party socialist state defined by defiance of the United States
Victory over a CIA-backed landing became the regime's founding myth of resistance
Soviet missiles brought the world to the nuclear brink; US pledged not to invade in exchange for withdrawal
Loss of subsidies shrank GDP by a third and taught survival through austerity and tourism
Embassies reopened briefly before Trump's first term reversed most openings
Largest protests since 1959 met with mass arrests; triggered record emigration of over a million people by 2024

keyEvents.event: Total grid collapses and island-wide blackouts
keyEvents.impact: Exposed the decay of power plants and dependence on Venezuelan oil

keyEvents.event: US oil blockade after Maduro's capture; repeated nationwide blackouts and first acknowledged talks with Washington
keyEvents.impact: Lost its Venezuelan oil lifeline; fuel ran out by May, hotels closed, US sanctioned Diaz-Canel personally and indicted Raul Castro

history.narrative: An aging revolutionary state that has survived six decades of US hostility on ideology, security-service control and foreign patrons. With Venezuelan oil gone and the grid collapsing, it is negotiating for the first time from near-total weakness while trying not to surrender the system itself.

redLines.description: US-imposed change of the constitution or of Communist Party rule
US military intervention or naval quarantine enforced by force against Cuban territory
Complete severance of the remaining fuel supply from Russia or Mexico

internalDivisions.name: Popular anger over blackouts, hunger and emigration vs. the party-state
Reformers seeking a market opening vs. orthodox Castro-era hardliners and GAESA military conglomerate

goals.description: Preserve Communist Party rule through the energy and economic collapse
Secure fuel imports by breaking or negotiating around the US oil blockade
Obtain sanctions relief through limited economic opening without political concessions
Keep Russian and Chinese backing as a counterweight to Washington
